2. The instant writ petition has been filed by the petitioner under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking for a direction to the respondents for referring the dispute regarding the amount of compensation of the land of the petitioners acquired for construction of BSF B.O.P to the learned L.A. Judge, North Tripura, Dharmanagar for determination of the rate and compensation in L.A.
Case No.7/D of 2008.
3.

Brief facts leading to this case are that the L.A. Collector, North Tripura, Dharmanagar (respondent No.3 herein) had issued a notice in the year 2008 to the petitioners regarding acquisition of land of the petitioners for construction of BSF B.O.P.

Pursuant to the notice issued by Md. Abu Taher Chowdhury vs Union Of India Represented By The ... on 13 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25744204/
1 respondent No.3, the petitioners had appeared at Ichailalcharra Tehsil with all relevant papers and documents of the acquired land of the petitioners.

sentences.text: Subsequently, an enquiry was carried out by the Revenue Inspector, Kadamtala Rev. Circle on the acquired land.

On 06.09.2010, respondent No.3 issued a notice to the petitioners to get the awarded amount of compensation of Rs.1,37,117/- and the same was accordingly received by the petitioners with a written objection dated 30.10.2010 addressed to the respondent No.3 stating that they were not in agreement in respect of the compensation amount as awarded for the acquired land and made a prayer to send the case to the competent court for proper adjudication under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; but till date the same has not been referred by the respondent No.3.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the inaction on part of the respondent No.3, the petitioners have filed the instant petition.

Hence,
this case.

4. Petitioners have prayed for the following reliefs:
"(I) Issue Writ/Writs to the Respondents or each of them as to why the Writ directing to refer the dispute regarding the proper assessment of the market value of the acquired land of the Petitioners at the time of acquisition and for proper assessment of compensation to the Ld' L.A. Judge, North Tripura, Kailashahar, at present Dharmanagar should not be passed.

AND (II) Issue Writ/Order directing the Respondents or each of them as to why such further direction and order should not be passed as per the prayer of the Petitioners.
AND (III) After hearing the parties Your Lordships would very kindly issue such Writ or Writs and order/orders directing the Respondents or each of them to refer the L.A.
Case vide No.7/D/2008, SL No.4 (Joint award) of the Petitioners to the Ld' L.A Judge, North Tripura, Dharmanagar u/s 18 of the L.A. Act 1894 within the specified period for assessment of the proper value of the compensation of the acquired land.
AND (IV) To issue further Writ/Writs or order or directions as Your Lordships deem fit and proper."
5.

Mr. D. Debnath, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, contends that the written objection was made by the petitioners way back in 2010 with a request to refer this case to the competent court regarding the amount of compensation as per the provision under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; but respondent No.3 has not yet taken any step insofar as referring the case to the competent court.

He also contends that in the year 2021, the petitioners made verbal communication to the office of the respondent No.3 with regard to referring their case under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, but all efforts were ended in smoke.

He further contends that the petitioners were waiting for the step to be taken by the respondent No.3 in referring their case to the competent court and this is the only reason for delay in filing the present petition.

Accordingly,
he prays for passing a direction to the respondent No.3 to refer the Case No.7/D of 2008 to the learned L.A. Judge, North Tripura, Dharmanagar under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 for assessment of the proper value of the compensation of the acquired land.

sentences.text:
On the other hand, Mr. P. Gautam, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.3,
vehemently objected the submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioners inter alia contending that there is an inordinate delay of long 13 years which cannot be lost sight of and prays for dismissal of the instant petition on the ground of delay and laches on part of the petitioners.
7. Having heard the submissions of the rival parties, this Court is of the considered view that there is an inordinate delay of about 13 years in filing the instant petition.

Moreover, since 2010, there was no written communication for referring their case with regard to the dissatisfaction of the awarded amount of the land acquired and mere verbal communications will not corroborate any ground to overlook the delay and laches made on behalf of the petitioners.
Thus, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners has failed to give any justifiable explanation for such delay and laches which are relevant in exercise of writ jurisdiction.
8. Accordingly, the writ petition being devoid of merit stands dismissed.
Pending application(s), if any, also stands disposed of.
